tldr: Non-English headlines overwhelmingly frame Buffett's departure as a business legend's end of era — 'Börsen-Legende', 'Fim de uma era', 'El arquitecto del capital moderno', 'el adiós definitivo' — while the majority of English-language titles deliver plain succession facts with no evaluative colour. BFM TV is the sole outlet whose headline leads with Buffett's own nepotism admission ('Il obtient ce poste parce qu'il est mon fils'), a framing invisible in every other title.

evidence.quote: Fim de uma era: Warren Buffett, o megainvestidor
a post he has held since 1970
net worth, son Howard in focus
Howard replaces his father, Warren Buffett
who will take over and what all will change

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline in the corpus to surface Buffett's nepotism admission verbatim — 'Il obtient ce poste parce qu'il est mon fils' (he gets this position because he's my son) — foregrounding the filial transaction where every other outlet, including all English-language press, used neutral succession language.
Only headline to title Buffett 'El arquitecto del capital moderno' (architect of modern capital) — the sole title treating the departure as a civilisational rather than corporate event.
Only headline to lead with 'Fim de uma era' (end of an era), framing the succession as a generational rupture; all English-language headlines in the corpus used neutral 'steps down' language.

Only headline to pair a celebrity label ('Börsen-Legende', stock-exchange legend) with Buffett's own farewell maxim ('Die Zeit gewinnt immer', time always wins) — the only title combining legendary status and mortality in a single line.
Used 'adiós definitivo' (definitive farewell) — the only Spanish-language headline to frame the departure as a permanent, irreversible exit rather than a governance transition.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, non-English outlets collectively advertise Buffett as a departing legend ending an era while most English-language titles strip the story to bare succession facts; BFM TV's nepotism-admission headline stands alone as the only title in the corpus that makes the filial transaction visible to the reader before the click.
